Late or Missed Assignments

If you need to miss a quiz/test/assignment, you must have a legitimate university approved excuse, such as a severe injury, illness, or participation in a legal proceeding that require your presence, etc. You must contact the instructor and provide satisfactory evidence prior to or within two days after the absence. A missed quiz/test/assignment without permission or supporting documents is a zero.

Note: Please note that we will not be able accept late submissions or reschedule exams due to personal trips or vacationing. 

Notify the instructor BEFORE an assignment is due if an urgent situation arises and you are unable to submit the assignment on time.

Fulton Schools of Engineering (FSE)  Academic Integrity Policy

Students in this class must adhere to ASU’s academic integrity policy, which can be found athttps://provost.asu.edu/academic-integrity/policy ). Students must review this policy and become familiar with each of the areas in which academic dishonesty can occur. All academic integrity violations will be reported to the Fulton Schools of Engineering Academic Integrity Office.  The Academic Integrity Office (AIO) maintains a record of all violations and has access to academic integrity violations committed in all other ASU colleges/schools. Course content, including lectures, are copyrighted materials. In addition to ASU’s academic integrity policy, students may not share outside the class, upload, sell or distribute course content or notes taken during the conduct of the course (see ACD 304–06, “Commercial Note Taking Services” for more information).

students must refrain from uploading to any course shell, discussion board, or website used by the course instructor or other course forum, material that is not the student's original work, unless the student first complies with all applicable copyright laws; faculty members reserve the right to delete materials on the grounds of suspected copyright infringement

Collaboration for Assignments

Unless otherwise instructed, you can discuss the assignments with other students and exchange ideas about how to solve them. However, there is a thin line between collaboration and plagiarizing the work of others, i.e. cheating. In order that you do not cross that line, you are required to compose your own unique solution to each of the problems. You cannot use any code or solution written by any of your classmates.

Some obvious acts of cheating are:

   * Turning in work/code done by someone else.

   * Copying work/code done by someone else.

   * Writing one code/solution together with someone else (it should be individual work).

All instances of cheating will be handled by the Dean's office according to the FSE Academic Integrity Policy listed above.

description_files_content.Operating_Systems_Assignment_Kernel_and_:
Arizona State University
CSE 330: Operating Systems
Assignment: Kernel Programming and CUDA
Instructions:
Answer all questions clearly and concisely. Include code snippets where appropriate. Use appropriate
system-level terminology and justify your answers based on kernel and CUDA principles.
1
1. Explain the difference between user space and kernel space. Why must device drivers operate
in kernel space?
2
2. Write a short C code snippet for a simple Linux kernel module that prints a message to the
system log when loaded and removed. Explain how it is compiled and loaded.
3
3. In CUDA programming, describe the differences between host memory and device memory.
How does memory transfer between these spaces occur?
4
4. Consider a CUDA kernel that computes the element-wise sum of two arrays. Write pseudocode
for the kernel function and explain how thread indexing is used.
5
5. Compare kernel synchronization mechanisms (such as semaphores or spinlocks) with CUDA
thread synchronization (e.g., __syncthreads()). When should each be used?
Submit your completed assignment as a single PDF file to the course portal. Include screenshots of
your kernel logs or CUDA output where relevant.
